definition: "Daisy Bell (Bicycle Built for Two)" is a song written in 1892 by British songwriter Harry Dacre with the chorus "Daisy, Daisy / Give me your answer, do.
details: / I'm half crazy / all for the love of you," ending with the words "a bicycle built for two." The song is said to have been inspired by Daisy Greville, Countess of Warwick, one of the many mistresses of King Edward VII. It is the earliest song sung using computer speech synthesis by the IBM 7090 in 1961.

explainer.lead: Daisy Bell is an 1892 song that became a computing landmark when an IBM 7090 sang it in 1961. The performance made a familiar popular tune the earliest song sung using computer speech synthesis.

tiers.eli5: Daisy Bell is an old song about loving someone and riding a bicycle built for two. In 1961, a big IBM computer sang it, a bit like teaching a talking machine to perform a tune everyone could recognize.
tiers.practitioner: For engineers, Daisy Bell is a historical reference point for computer-generated sung speech rather than an implementation to reproduce. Cite the IBM 7090 performance of 1961 as an early demonstration, not as a description of a particular synthesis pipeline or toolset.
tiers.paperLevel: The historical relation can be written as: song(Harry Dacre, 1892) → computer-synthesized performance(IBM 7090, 1961). Its significance is that of an early speech-synthesis milestone, not a named synthesis model or algorithm.

explainer.example: An IBM 7090 singing the chorus line “Daisy, Daisy / Give me your answer, do” in 1961 turned Dacre's nineteenth-century song into a demonstration of computer speech synthesis.

usedIn.name: Computer speech synthesis
usedIn.detail: The performance serves as an early historical demonstration of a computer singing.

explainer.intuition: A well-known song gives listeners an easy way to recognize a technical achievement: instead of merely producing sound, a computer performed words and music people already knew.
howItWorks: Harry Dacre wrote Daisy Bell, also called Bicycle Built for Two, in 1892.
Its chorus addresses Daisy and ends with the phrase a bicycle built for two.
In 1961, the IBM 7090 performed the song using computer speech synthesis.
That performance made it the earliest song sung in this way.
explainer.whyItMatters: Daisy Bell links popular music with an early milestone in synthesized speech, giving the technology a memorable and easily recognized place in computing history.
misconceptions: The song was not written by a computer or by IBM; Harry Dacre wrote it in 1892.
Daisy Greville, Countess of Warwick, is said to have inspired it, rather than being a confirmed inspiration.
The 1961 performance identifies the computer and achievement, not a detailed synthesis method.
